To address this, we can use the backdoor criterion to identify the causal effect of Zuph on Glimx. The backdoor path is Zuph -> Jyka -> Glimx. However, since Jyka is a direct effect of Zuph, conditioning on Jyka will not block the backdoor path.

We can use the given probabilities to calculate the probability of Glimx given Zuph, P(Glimx|Zuph), and the probability of Glimx given ¬Zuph, P(Glimx|¬Zuph). 

Comparing the two probabilities, we see that P(Glimx|Zuph) > P(Glimx|¬Zuph). This suggests that the presence of Zuph increases the probability of Glimx.
